claim: Leptin robustly suppresses food intake by acting upon the leptin receptor (LepR) signaling system residing within the agouti-related protein (AgRP) neurons of the hypothalamus.
source: The hormone leptin is known to robustly suppress food intake by acting upon the leptin receptor (LepR) signaling system residing within the agouti-related protein (AgRP) neurons of the hypothalamus.
evidence: This claim is supported by established scientific knowledge and citations in the literature about leptin's mechanism of action.

claim: Clinical studies indicate that leptin is undesirable as a therapeutic regiment for obesity.
source: However, clinical studies indicate that leptin is undesirable as a therapeutic regiment for obesity, which is at least partly attributed to the poorly understood complex secondary structure and key signaling mechanism of the leptin-responsive neural circuit.
evidence: This claim references clinical studies that have evaluated leptin as a therapeutic option.

claim: LepR-expressing portal neurons send GABAergic projections to a cohort of α3-GABAA receptor expressing neurons within the dorsomedial hypothalamic nucleus (DMH) for the control of leptin-mediated obesity phenotype.
source: Here, we show that the LepR-expressing portal neurons send GABAergic projections to a cohort of α3-GABAA receptor expressing neurons within the dorsomedial hypothalamic nucleus (DMH) for the control of leptin-mediated obesity phenotype.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The DMH is a key brain region that contributes to the regulation of leptin-mediated feeding.
source: We identified the DMH as a key brain region that contributes to the regulation of leptin-mediated feeding.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing the role of DMH in leptin-mediated feeding regulation.

claim: Acute activation of the GABAergic AgRP-DMH circuit promoted food intake and glucose intolerance.
source: Acute activation of the GABAergic AgRP-DMH circuit promoted food intake and glucose intolerance, while activation of post-synaptic MC4R neurons in the DMH elicited exactly opposite phenotypes.
evidence: This claim is supported by optogenetic experiments shown in Figure 4A and 4B.

claim: Activation of post-synaptic MC4R neurons in the DMH decreased food intake and improved glucose tolerance.
source: Acute activation of the GABAergic AgRP-DMH circuit promoted food intake and glucose intolerance, while activation of post-synaptic MC4R neurons in the DMH elicited exactly opposite phenotypes.
evidence: This claim is supported by optogenetic experiments shown in Figure 4C and 4D.

claim: Rapid deletion of LepR from AgRP neurons caused an obesity phenotype which can be rescued by blockage of GABAA receptor in the DMH.
source: Rapid deletion of LepR from AgRP neurons caused an obesity phenotype which can be rescued by blockage of GABAA receptor in the DMH.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1 and Figure 4.

claim: DMH neurons displayed suppressed neural activities in response to hunger or hyperglycemia.
source: Consistent with behavioral results, these DMH neurons displayed suppressed neural activities in response to hunger or hyperglycemia.
evidence: This claim is supported by in vivo electrophysiology data shown in Figure 4L-Q.

claim: α3-GABAA receptor signaling within the DMH exerts potent bi-directional regulation of the central effects of leptin on feeding and body weight.
source: Furthermore, we identified that α3-GABAA receptor signaling within the DMH exerts potent bi-directional regulation of the central effects of leptin on feeding and body weight.
evidence: This claim is supported by genetic manipulation experiments shown in Figure 5.

claim: Diet-induced obesity (DIO) drastically increases susceptibility to the development of metabolic, cardiovascular, and neurological diseases, as well as the recent coronavirus disease.
source: Diet-induced obesity (DIO) drastically increases susceptibility to the development of metabolic, cardiovascular, and neurological diseases, as well as the recent coronavirus disease (Kahn et al., 2006; Ren et al., 2021; Clemmensen et al., 2020; Xia et al., 2021; Benito-León et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Leptin interacts with receptors in the brain to communicate peripheral fuel status, suppress appetite following a meal, promote energy expenditure, and maintain blood glucose stability.
source: Leptin, a hormone secreted by white adipocytes, interacts with receptors in the brain to communicate peripheral fuel status, suppress appetite following a meal, promote energy expenditure, and maintain blood glucose stability (Friedman, 2009; Friedman, 2014; Flak and Myers, 2016; Friedman, 2019; Knight et al., 2010; Berglund et al., 2012; Caron et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to established research on leptin function.

claim: One of the key pathological characteristics of DIO is impaired metabolic homeostasis.
source: One of the key pathological characteristics of DIO is impaired metabolic homeostasis (Considine et al., 1995; Maffei et al., 1995).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Central leptin signaling plays a vital role in the regulation of body weight, primarily via action within the arcuate nucleus (ARC).
source: There is much evidence that central leptin signaling plays a vital role in the regulation of body weight, primarily via action within the arcuate nucleus (ARC)(Friedman, 2014; Flak and Myers, 2016; Minokoshi et al., 2002; Huynh et al., 2010; Pereira et al., 2019; Xu et al., 2018; Varela and Horvath, 2012; Vong et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: The long-form leptin receptors are abundantly expressed in the agouti-related protein (AgRP) neurons of the ARC.
source: The long-form leptin receptors are abundantly expressed in the agouti-related protein (AgRP) neurons of the ARC (Xu et al., 2018; Baskin et al., 1999; Xu and Xie, 2016; Scott et al., 2009; Scott et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Under the physiological condition, leptin directly inhibits leptin receptor (LepR)-expressing AgRP neurons.
source: Previous studies demonstrate that, under the physiological condition, leptin directly inhibits leptin receptor (LepR)-expressing AgRP neurons (Cowley et al., 2001; van den Top et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Clinical studies suggest that treatment of leptin in common obese patients has limited efficacy.
source: However, clinical studies suggest that treatment of leptin in common obese patients has limited efficacy (Heymsfield et al., 1999; Farr et al., 2015; Hinney et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to clinical studies.

claim: AgRP neurons play fundamental roles in regulating feeding behavior and body weight by releasing inhibitory neuropeptide Y (NPY), AgRP and GABA transmitters into many downstream brain areas.
source: AgRP neurons play fundamental roles in regulating feeding behavior and body weight by releasing inhibitory neuropeptide Y (NPY), AgRP and GABA transmitters into many downstream brain areas (Kishi and Elmquist, 2005; Han et al., 2021b; Xia et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The afferents to AgRP neurons and their postsynaptic targets have been identified as key players in the regulation of energy balance and systemic insulin sensitivity.
source: The afferents to these AgRP neurons and their postsynaptic targets have been identified as key players in the regulation of energy balance and systemic insulin sensitivity (Myers et al., 2009; Gropp et al., 2005; Luquet et al., 2005; Aponte et al., 2011; Könner et al., 2007; Steculorum et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Leptin acts to decrease food intake and promote energy expenditure by suppressing the activity of AgRP neurons.
source: Leptin acts to decrease food intake and promote energy expenditure by suppressing the activity of AgRP neurons (Cowley et al., 2001; van den Top et al., 2004; Halaas et al., 1997; Friedman and Halaas, 1998).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Selective ablation of LepR in AgRP neurons gives rise to an obese phenotype and diabetes.
source: Selective ablation of LepR in AgRP neurons gives rise to an obese phenotype and diabetes (Xu et al., 2018; van de Wall et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: GABA signaling plays a critical role in the control of feeding behavior and energy homeostasis.
source: Emerging data suggest a critical role of GABA signaling on the control of feeding behavior and energy homeostasis (Vong et al., 2011; Cone, 2005; Meister, 2007; Morton et al., 2006; Saper et al., 2002; Wu and Palmiter, 2011; Liu et al., 2012; Wu et al., 2013; Wu et al., 2009; Wu et al., 2012; Rossi and Stuber, 2018; Richard, 2015; Meng et al., 2016; Garfield et al., 2016; Pool et al., 2014; Cai et al., 2014; Krashes et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Central GABAA- and GABAB-receptor signaling exert prominent influences on feeding behavior under various metabolic states.
source: Numerous studies suggest that central GABAA- and GABAB-receptor signaling exert prominent influences on feeding behavior under various metabolic states (Berridge, 2009; Cooper, 2005; Duke et al., 2006; Martire et al., 2010; Peciña and Berridge, 1996; Strader et al., 1997; Berner et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Pharmacological activation of GABAA-receptor signaling in the hindbrain parabrachial nucleus (PBN) enhances the positive hedonic perception of tastes and foods, thereby promoting food intake and motivational response to food reward.
source: For example, pharmacological activation of GABAA-receptor signaling in the hindbrain parabrachial nucleus (PBN) enhances the positive hedonic perception of tastes and foods, thereby promoting food intake and motivational response to food reward (Berridge, 2009; Cooper, 2005; Peciña and Berridge, 1996; Berridge and Peciña, 1995; Higgs and Cooper, 1996; Söderpalm and Berridge, 2000; Berridge and Treit, 1986).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: GABAergic signaling from AgRP neurons plays a bidirectional, post-developmental role in the regulation of food intake and body weight.
source: Utilizing advanced genetic techniques, we have shown that GABAergic signaling from AgRP neurons plays a bidirectional, post-developmental role in the regulation of food intake and body weight (Meng et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior research by the authors.

claim: The α5-containing GABAA receptor signaling within the bed nucleus of the stria terminalis neurons reciprocally regulates mental disorders and obesity.
source: Our recent work shows that the α5-containing GABAA receptor signaling within the bed nucleus of the stria terminalis neurons reciprocally regulates mental disorders and obesity, implying that GABAA-receptor signaling exerts a role in controlling obesity and comorbid diseases (Xia et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior research by the authors.

claim: Agrp-Lepr KO mice showed a significant increase in feeding and body weight one week after deletion of LepR signaling from AgRP neurons.
source: Agrp-Lepr KO mice showed a significant increase in feeding and body weight one week after deletion of LepR signaling from AgRP neurons (Figure 1G and H).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1G and H.

claim: Agrp-Lepr KO mice exhibited 44.5% increase in feeding as compared to the control mice.
source: As a recapitulation of the severe hyperphagia caused by CRISPR-mediated LepR deletion (Xu et al., 2018), our Agrp-Lepr KO mice exhibited 44.5% increase in feeding as compared to the control mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and comparison to prior research.

claim: Agrp-Lepr KO mice exhibited impaired glucose tolerance.
source: Furthermore, along with the increase of body weight and food intake, Agrp-Lepr KO mice exhibited impaired glucose tolerance (Figure 1I).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1I.

claim: Chronic infusion of bicuculline into the 3rd ventricle abolished the hyperphagia responses in Agrp-Lepr KO mice.
source: Intriguingly, chronic infusion of bicuculline (Bic, 1 ng, a GABAA receptor antagonist) into the 3rd ventricle abolished the hyperphagia responses in Agrp-Lepr KO mice (Figure 1J), suggesting that facilitating the post-synaptic GABAA signaling to the AgRP neural circuit is important in regulating leptin-mediated feeding.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1J.

claim: The feeding efficiency was significantly higher in Agrp-Lepr KO mice but was rescued by infusion of Bic.
source: The feeding efficiency (body weight gain [mg]/kilocalorie consumed) was significantly higher in Agrp-Lepr KO mice but was rescued by infusion of Bic (Figure 1K).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1K.

claim: The expansion of white adipose tissue (WAT) was observed in Agrp-Lepr KO mice.
source: The expansion of white adipose tissue (WAT) was observed in Agrp-Lepr KO mice (Figure 1L).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1L.

claim: A significant decrease in respiratory quotient (RQ) was observed from the Agrp-Lepr KO mice that can be further normalized by infusion of GABAA antagonist.
source: We observed a significant decrease in respiratory quotient (RQ) from the Agrp-Lepr KO mice that can be further normalized by infusion of GABAA antagonist (Figure 1M).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1M.

claim: Ablation of LepR in the AgRP neurons impaired glucose tolerance, which was fully restored by infusion of GABAA antagonist.
source: Ablation of LepR in the AgRP neurons impaired glucose tolerance, which was fully restored by infusion of GABAA antagonist (Figure 1N).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1N.

claim: Leptin regulates feeding and energy metabolism via post-synaptic GABAA signaling from AgRP neurons.
source: These results indicate that leptin regulates feeding and energy metabolism via post-synaptic GABAA signaling from AgRP neurons.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental results presented in Figure 1.

claim: Rapid deletion of LepR signaling from AgRP neurons resulted in a significant decrease of Npas4 abundance within the DMH.
source: The qPCR results showed that rapid deletion of LepR signaling from AgRP neurons resulted in a significant decrease of Npas4 abundance within the DMH (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Neonatal ablation of AgRP neurons significantly diminished the leptin-mediated Fos induction within post-synaptic neurons residing in the DMH.
source: However, neonatal ablation of AgRP neurons significantly diminished the leptin-mediated Fos induction within post-synaptic neurons residing in the DMH (Figure 2C–F and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 2C-F.

claim: The DMH is the key downstream target that critically contributes to the regulation of leptin-mediated appetitive and metabolic responses.
source: These results suggest that the DMH could be the key downstream target that critically contributes to the regulation of leptin-mediated appetitive and metabolic responses.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the Npas4 and Fos expression data.

claim: ~17% (CTB tracing) or 39% (HSV tracing) of AgRP neurons project to the DMH.
source: Both HSV-based retrograde tracing and cholera toxin subunit B (CTB)-based retrograde neuroanatomical tracing from the DMH showed that ~17% (CTB tracing) or 39% (HSV tracing) of AgRP neurons project to the DMH (Figure 2H–L and Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by retrograde tracing data shown in Figure 2H-L and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: ~78% of AgRP-targeted neurons in the DMH express melanocortin receptor 4 (MC4R).
source: RNA in situ hybridization confirmed that ~78% of AgRP-targeted neurons in the DMH express melanocortin receptor 4 (MC4R) (Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Inhibitory postsynaptic currents (IPSCs) in the DMH neurons triggered by photostimulation of ChR2-expressing axonal terminals of AgRP neurons were fully blocked by Bic.
source: We observed that inhibitory postsynaptic currents (IPSCs) in the DMH neurons triggered by photostimulation of ChR2-expressing axonal terminals of AgRP neurons were fully blocked by Bic (Figure 3D and E), confirming that these terminals were releasing GABA.
evidence: This claim is supported by electrophysiology data shown in Figure 3D and E.

claim: Photostimulation of the ChR2-expressing AgRP terminals resulted in inhibition of action potentials in postsynaptic ZsGreen-positive neurons of the DMH in a reversible manner with significant reduction of firing rate and resting membrane potential.
source: In the presence of DNQX (a competitive AMPA/kainate receptor antagonist), AP5 (a selective NMDA receptor antagonist) and Bic, photostimulation of the ChR2-expressing AgRP terminals resulted in inhibition of action potentials in postsynaptic ZsGreen-positive neurons of the DMH in a reversible manner with significant reduction of firing rate and resting membrane potential (Figure 3F–I).
evidence: This claim is supported by electrophysiology data shown in Figure 3F-I.

claim: Systemic treatment of leptin significantly enhanced neural activities of DMH neurons.
source: We further examined the effect of leptin on the firing of postsynaptic ZsGreen-positive neurons in the DMH. We found that systemic treatment of leptin significantly enhanced neural activities of DMH neurons (Figure 3J and K).
evidence: This claim is supported by electrophysiology data shown in Figure 3J and K.

claim: Photostimulation of AgRP fibers in the DMH promoted feeding and impaired glucose tolerance.
source: Photostimulation of AgRP fibers in the DMH promoted feeding and impaired glucose tolerance (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by optogenetic experiments shown in Figure 4A and B.

claim: About 13% of DMH neurons could be sensitive to the activation of AgRP neurons.
source: We found that about 13% of DMH neurons could be sensitive to the activation of AgRP neurons (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by Fos expression data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Photostimulation of post-synaptic MC4RDMH neurons decreased feeding and improved glucose tolerance.
source: In contrast, photostimulation of post-synaptic MC4RDMH neurons decreased feeding and improved glucose tolerance (Figure 4C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by optogenetic experiments shown in Figure 4C and D.

claim: Bilateral infusion of Bic into the DMH of Agrp-Lepr KO mice resulted in reduced feeding and a significant reduction of body weight, coupled with improved glucose tolerance.
source: Bilateral infusion of Bic (4 ng) into the DMH of Agrp-Lepr KO mice with micro-osmotic pumps resulted in reduced feeding and a significant reduction of body weight, coupled with improved glucose tolerance (Figure 4E–G).
evidence: This claim is supported by pharmacological experiments shown in Figure 4E-G.

claim: Blockage of GABAA receptor in the DMH significantly rescued the feeding efficiency, expansion of WAT, and the RQ profiles in Agrp-Lepr KO mice.
source: Blockage of GABAA receptor in the DMH significantly rescued the feeding efficiency, expansion of WAT, and the RQ profiles in Agrp-Lepr KO mice (Figure 4H–K).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4H-K.

claim: GABAA receptor signaling in the DMH is critical for the feeding, body weight, and glucose tolerance regulated by LepR in AgRP neurons.
source: These results suggest that GABAA receptor signaling in the DMH is critical for the feeding, body weight, and glucose tolerance regulated by LepR in AgRP neurons.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental results in Figure 4.

claim: 10 out of 16 identified MC4R neurons showed decreased firing rate during foraging (prior to meal initiation), with an average reduction of firing rate from 9.8 Hz to 5.1 Hz.
source: The results showed that 10 out of 16 identified MC4R neurons showed decreased firing rate during foraging (prior to meal initiation), with an average reduction of firing rate from 9.8 Hz to 5.1 Hz (Figure 4L, M and P).
evidence: This claim is supported by in vivo electrophysiology data shown in Figure 4L, M and P.

claim: 10 out of 16 MC4R neurons responded to the enhancement of blood glucose with a reduction of firing rate from 10.0 Hz to 7.1 Hz.
source: We also observed 10 out of 16 MC4R neurons that responded to the enhancement of blood glucose with a reduction of firing rate from 10.0 Hz to 7.1 Hz (Figure 4N, O and Q).
evidence: This claim is supported by in vivo electrophysiology data shown in Figure 4N, O and Q.

claim: Among all major regulatory α subunits, the transcript level of Gabra3 (encoding GABAA receptor α3 subunits) in the DMH neurons of Agrp-Lepr KO mice was the highest.
source: Results of qPCR analysis showed that, among all major regulatory α subunits, the transcript level of Gabra3 (encoding GABAA receptor α3 subunits) in the DMH neurons of Agrp-Lepr KO mice was the highest (Figure 5A).
evidence: This claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: α3-GABAA was abundantly expressed within the DMH.
source: Immunostaining confirmed that α3-GABAA was abundantly expressed within the DMH (Figure 5B).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The α3-GABAA signaling was highly co-localized within the post-synaptic targets of the AgRP→DMH neural circuit.
source: Our transsynaptic tracing study further confirmed that the α3-GABAA signaling was highly co-localized within the post-synaptic targets of the AgRP→DMH neural circuit (Figure 5C–E).
evidence: This claim is supported by transsynaptic tracing data shown in Figure 5C-E.

claim: Knockout of Gabra3 signaling in the MC4RDMH neurons reduced feeding and body weight while glucose tolerance was significantly improved.
source: We found that knockout of Gabra3 signaling in the MC4RDMH neurons reduced feeding and body weight while glucose tolerance was significantly improved (Figure 5F–H and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by genetic manipulation experiments shown in Figure 5F-H.

claim: Deficiency in α3-GABAA signaling significantly decreased feeding efficiency and WAT.
source: Deficiency in α3-GABAA signaling also significantly decreased feeding efficiency and WAT (Figure 5I and J).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5I and J.

claim: Overexpression of α3-GABAA within the MC4RDMH neurons manifested opposite phenotypes, including moderately increased feeding and body weight and significantly increased feeding efficiency and WAT adiposity.
source: A gain-of-function study showed that overexpression of α3-GABAA within the same MC4RDMH neurons manifested opposite phenotypes, including moderately increased feeding and body weight and significantly increased feeding efficiency and WAT adiposity (Figure 5F–J).
evidence: This claim is supported by genetic manipulation experiments shown in Figure 5F-J.

claim: Overexpression of α3-GABAA in the DMH neurons blunted the actions of leptin on feeding, body weight, glucose tolerance, feeding efficiency, and WAT adiposity.
source: Importantly, overexpression of α3-GABAA in the DMH neurons blunted the actions of leptin on feeding, body weight, glucose tolerance, feeding efficiency, and WAT adiposity (Figure 5K–O).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5K-O.

claim: Knockout of Gabra3 signaling in the MC4RDMH neurons abolished the enhancement of feeding and impairment of glucose tolerance during activation of AgRP-DMH circuit.
source: We found that knockout of Gabra3 signaling in the MC4RDMH neurons abolished the enhancement of feeding and impairment of glucose tolerance during activation of AgRP-DMH circuit (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by optogenetic experiments combined with genetic manipulation shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: The AgRP-DMH circuit regulates feeding and glucose tolerance depending on the α3-GABAA receptor signaling in the MC4RDMH neurons.
source: These results suggest the AgRP-DMH circuit regulates feeding and glucose tolerance depending on the α3-GABAA receptor signaling in the MC4RDMH neurons.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental results in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: Genetic deletion of Gabra3 signaling in the MC4RDMH neurons led to a decrease in daily food consumption associated with a moderate weight loss in diet-induced obese mice.
source: We found that genetic deletion of Gabra3 signaling in the MC4RDMH neurons led to a decrease in daily food consumption associated with a moderate weight loss and that these knockout mice showed reduced refeeding responses (Figure 5P–R).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data in diet-induced obese mice shown in Figure 5P-R.

claim: The MC4RDMH neurons play a significant role in control of glucose tolerance and feeding through the α3-GABAA signaling.
source: These results suggest that the MC4RDMH neurons play a significant role in control of glucose tolerance and feeding through the α3-GABAA signaling.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental results in Figure 5.

claim: The newly established inducible-knockout strategy achieves rapid, post-developmental, targeted inactivation of LepR signaling.
source: This study utilized a newly established inducible-knockout strategy to achieve rapid, post-developmental, targeted inactivation of LepR signaling, which precisely illuminates the pathophysiological roles of central leptin signaling on the control of nutrient partitioning and feeding efficiency.
evidence: This claim describes the methodology used in the study.

claim: The Agrp-Lepr KO model showed a robust disruption in various feeding and metabolism parameters, culminating in severe obesity.
source: Compared with the mild effects of the non-inducible manipulation of brain LepR signaling, our Agrp-Lepr KO model showed a robust disruption in various feeding and metabolism parameters, culminating in severe obesity, which was previously achieved by global genetic deletion or the CRISPR–Cas9 technique (Xu et al., 2018; van de Wall et al., 2008; Gonçalves et al., 2014; Egan et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim compares the current model to previous approaches and is supported by data and citations.

claim: HSV-hEF1α has been extensively used to retrogradely transport from the peripheral nerve terminals to the central nervous system through axonal transport.
source: HSV-hEF1α has been extensively used to retrogradely transport from the peripheral nerve terminals to the central nervous system through axonal transport (Fang et al., 2018; Tan et al., 2016; Eagle et al., 2020; Yamaguchi et al., 2020; Garcia et al., 2021; Gremel et al., 2016; Valentinova et al., 2019; Marcinkiewcz et al., 2016), while some applications take advantage of the anterograde capacity of other different strains for example HSV-H129 (Azevedo et al., 2019; Lo and Anderson, 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations describing the use of HSV for tracing.

claim: CTB is capable of being taken up by neurons and transported in a retrograde direction towards the cell body.
source: To further verify the AgRP-DMH circuit, we applied CTB which is capable of being taken up by neurons and transported in a retrograde direction towards the cell body.
evidence: This claim describes the properties of CTB as a retrograde tracer, which is established knowledge.

claim: Pharmacological blockage of GABAA signaling within the AgRP-DMH circuit can blunt the hyperphagia responses and improve glucose intolerance in Agrp-Lepr KO mice.
source: We applied pharmacological approaches to block GABAA signaling within the AgRP-DMH circuit, which can blunt the hyperphagia responses and improve glucose intolerance in Agrp-Lepr KO mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1 and Figure 4.

claim: The GABAA signaling system within the AgRP-DMH circuit exerts rapid actions on feeding behaviors and glucose metabolism.
source: These results suggest that the GABAA signaling system within the AgRP-DMH circuit exerts rapid actions on feeding behaviors and glucose metabolism.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the pharmacological experiments.

claim: Chronic blockage of GABAA signaling in the DMH resulted in decreased food intake and weight loss.
source: Furthermore, we observed decreased food intake and weight loss as a result of chronic blockage of GABAA signaling in the DMH, indicating that GABAA signaling within the AgRP-DMH circuit may also participate in the chronic regulation of feeding and body weight.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from chronic infusion experiments.

claim: AgRP neurons can chronically regulate feeding through the mechanism of long-term suppression over the downstream brain targets independent of GABAA signaling.
source: On the other hand, some studies showed that AgRP neurons can chronically regulate feeding through the mechanism of long-term suppression over the downstream brain targets independent of GABAA signaling (Krashes et al., 2013; Wang et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The GABA signaling in the AgRP neurons may exert chronic effects on appetite and weight control via a distinct neural pathway from the co-released AgRP and NPY.
source: Together, we suggest that the GABA signaling in the AgRP neurons may exert chronic effects on appetite and weight control via a distinct neural pathway from the co-released AgRP and NPY.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the experimental results and prior research.

claim: Among various downstream targets of the AgRP circuit, the DMH neurons are the most sensitive to AgRP-dependent leptin signaling.
source: The profiling assay using neonatal ablation of AgRP neurons revealed key neural populations responding to leptin. Among various downstream targets of the AgRP circuit, the DMH neurons are the most sensitive to AgRP-dependent leptin signaling.
evidence: This claim is supported by the Npas4 and Fos expression profiling data.

claim: Acute stimulation of post-synaptic MC4R neurons within the DMH blunted glucose tolerance and feeding.
source: Acute stimulation of post-synaptic MC4R neurons within the DMH blunted glucose tolerance and feeding.
evidence: This claim is supported by optogenetic experiments shown in Figure 4C and D.

claim: The GABAA subunits α3 within the secondary structure of the GABAergic neural circuit play an important role in the control of leptin-mediated hypometabolism and obesity.
source: These studies demonstrate that the GABAA subunits α3 within the secondary structure of the GABAergic neural circuit play an important role in the control of leptin-mediated hypometabolism and obesity.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the genetic manipulation experiments in Figure 5.

claim: 62.5% of MC4R neurons in the DMH neurons are relevant to hyperglycemia due to their suppressed neural activity associated with high glucose levels.
source: Our results showed that 62.5% of MC4R neurons in the DMH neurons are relevant to hyperglycemia due to their suppressed neural activity associated with high glucose levels.
evidence: This claim is supported by in vivo electrophysiology data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Glucose is a complex and dynamic metabolic signal that interacts with multiple neural circuits to regulate glucose homeostasis.
source: Overall, the effects of glucose on MC4R neurons in the DMH suggest that glucose is a complex and dynamic metabolic signal that interacts with multiple neural circuits to regulate glucose homeostasis.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the electrophysiology results and general knowledge.

claim: LepR in the AgRP neurons and the associated neural circuit and receptor are the primary mediators of leptin action in feeding and metabolic homeostasis.
source: In conclusion, LepR in the AgRP neurons and the associated neural circuit and receptor are the primary mediators of leptin action in feeding and metabolic homeostasis.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from all the experimental results in the study.

claim: New therapeutics selectively targeting α3-GABAA associated signaling components within this GABAergic neural circuit would prevent obesity.
source: We suggest that new therapeutics selectively targeting α3-GABAA associated signaling components within this GABAergic neural circuit would prevent obesity.
evidence: This is a speculative suggestion based on the study's findings.

claim: Npas4 has a more dynamic response to activity-dependent signaling via Ca2+, and it can be bidirectionally regulated by either excitatory or inhibitory input.
source: Traditional immediate early genes are regulated by neuromodulators via cAMP, neurotrophins, and other paracrine factors, and their kinetics are relatively slow. In contrast, Npas4 has a more dynamic response to activity-dependent signaling via Ca2+, and it can be bidirectionally regulated by either excitatory or inhibitory input (Shepard et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior research on Npas4.

claim: Without ablation of AgRP neurons, leptin induced robust Fos expression in almost all major targets of AgRP neurons.
source: Without ablation of AgRP neurons, leptin induced robust Fos expression in almost all major targets of AgRP neurons (Wu et al., 2009; Wu et al., 2012; Wu et al., 2008b).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: There are several brain regions such as ARC, LH, PVH, VMH, and DMH that could sense peripheral glucose levels including glucose-excited and glucose-inhibited neurons.
source: There are several brain regions such as ARC, LH, PVH, VMH, and DMH that could sense peripheral glucose levels including glucose-excited and glucose-inhibited neurons (Routh et al., 2014; Claret et al., 2007; He et al., 2020; Huang et al., 2022; Burdakov et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research on glucose-sensing neurons.

claim: The neural circuit from LepR-expressing AgRP neurons to α3-GABAA receptor expressing DMH neurons plays a critical role in the control of feeding, body weight and glucose tolerance through α3-GABAA receptor signaling.
source: We identified and characterized a unique GABAergic neural circuit with functional significance: the neural circuit from LepR-expressing AgRP neurons to α3-GABAA receptor expressing DMH neurons plays a critical role in the control of feeding, body weight and glucose tolerance through α3-GABAA receptor signaling.
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings of the study supported by all experimental data.

evidence: This is an inference drawn from chronic infusion experiments.

claim: Leptin induces phosphorylation of signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (pSTAT3).
source: Leptin induces phosphorylation of signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (pSTAT3). pSTAT3 staining in the ARC showed enhanced extent in control mice but not in Agrp-Lepr KO mice 1  hr after leptin treatment in overnight fasted mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 2), indicating the role of leptin in the ARC was ablated.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.
